// Code generated by msx2go. DO NOT EDIT.

// Command __NAME__-play runs the translated cartridge in a window.
//
// Ebiten, so the same source builds for desktop and for the browser:
//
//	go build -tags msxdata ./cmd/__NAME__-play
//	GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build -tags msxdata -o game.wasm ./cmd/__NAME__-play
//
// A browser build must have the data compiled in -- there is no filesystem to
// look in -- which is what the msxdata tag is for.
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"image"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"
	eaudio "github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2/audio"

	"__MODULE__/z80"
)

func main() {
	data := flag.String("data", "", "where to find __NAME__.dat")
	scale := flag.Int("scale", 3, "window scale")
	state := flag.String("state", "", "where snapshots go (default "+
		"<cartridge>.state). F9 saves, F10 restores")
	learn := flag.String("learn", "", "write every address that had to run "+
		"interpreted here on exit, in the form msx2go -sites reads; "+
		"append it to the module's sites.txt and regenerate")
	disk := flag.String("disk", "", "where a changed floppy is written on "+
		"exit (default <name>.dsk). Only for disk builds")
	full := flag.Bool("fullscreen", false, "start filling the screen. F11 "+
		"toggles it at any time")
	border := flag.Bool("border", true, "draw the border the hardware draws "+
		"around the picture, in the colour register 7 sets. The image "+
		"itself is already 4:3 with square pixels, so this is what a "+
		"television showed that a bare framebuffer does not")
	cpu := flag.Float64("cpu", 1, "how fast the processor is, as a multiple "+
		"of a stock MSX. At 1 a handler that does more work than a frame "+
		"has cycles for overruns and the game loses its next interrupt, "+
		"which is what the hardware does and what the game was tuned "+
		"around. Raise it and the game runs every frame -- smoother, and "+
		"faster. A negative value turns the accounting off entirely.")
	speed := flag.Float64("speed", 1, "wall-clock speed, as a multiple. 0.5 "+
		"is half speed, 2 is double. It changes how fast the machine is "+
		"driven, not what kind of machine it is")
	rec := flag.String("rectape", "", "record what is pressed, one byte a "+
		"frame, and write it here on exit. Replay it with msxrun -btape "+
		"to reproduce a session exactly")
	sndCart := flag.String("sndcart", "", "put a Konami sound cartridge in "+
		"a slot: \"scc\" or \"scc+\". A game with no cartridge of its "+
		"own -- one booted from a disk -- reaches the chip this way, "+
		"and looks for it in the slot the hardware left free")
	hz := flag.Int("hz", 60, "the machine's vertical frequency: 60 for a "+
		"Japanese or American MSX, 50 for a European one. It sets both "+
		"the rate the machine is driven at and what the cartridge is "+
		"told when it asks, which have to agree")
	flag.Parse()

	m, err := z80.Cartridge.Open(*data)
	if err != nil {
		die(err)
	}
	m.CPUScale = *cpu
	m.LearnSites = *learn != ""
	if *speed <= 0 {
		die(fmt.Errorf("-speed must be positive"))
	}
	if *hz != 50 && *hz != 60 {
		die(fmt.Errorf("-hz must be 50 or 60, not %d", *hz))
	}
	m.Hz = *hz
	switch *sndCart {
	case "":
	case "scc":
		if err := m.SoundCartIn(2, false); err != nil {
			die(err)
		}
	case "scc+":
		if err := m.SoundCartIn(2, true); err != nil {
			die(err)
		}
	default:
		die(fmt.Errorf("-sndcart wants %q or %q, not %q",
			"scc", "scc+", *sndCart))
	}
	if err := z80.Cartridge.Start(m, z80.Base); err != nil {
		die(err)
	}
	m.SCC.SetSampleRate(sampleRate)
	if *state == "" {
		*state = z80.Cartridge.Name + ".state"
	}
	// One frame of sound is the sample rate divided by the frames a second
	// the machine is being run at, which is what -hz and -speed set.
	g := &game{m: m, rend: z80.NewRenderer(),
		snd:    newSound(m, int(float64(sampleRate)/(float64(*hz)**speed))),
		state:  *state,
		border: *border}
	startAudio(g.snd)
	if n := m.Images(); n > 1 {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "__NAME__: %d floppies; F12 inserts the "+
			"next one. %s is in the drive.\n", n, m.ImageName(m.Mounted(0)))
	}

	w, h := z80.ScreenWidth, z80.ScreenHeight
	if *border {
		w, h = z80.FrameWidth, z80.FrameHeight
	}
	ebiten.SetWindowSize(w**SCALE**, h**SCALE**)
	ebiten.SetWindowTitle(z80.Cartridge.Name)
	ebiten.SetTPS(int(float64(*hz) * *speed))
	// Ebiten scales the layout to the display and keeps its proportions,
	// so a full screen letterboxes the picture rather than stretching it.
	ebiten.SetFullscreen(*full)
	g.rec = *rec != ""
	err = ebiten.RunGame(g)
	// The tape of what was pressed, so a session can be replayed
	// frame for frame. A fault seen once by a person playing is a
	// fault that can be measured afterwards.
	if g.rec {
		if e := os.WriteFile(*rec, g.tape, 0o644); e != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%s: %v\n", z80.Cartridge.Name, e)
		} else {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%s: wrote %d frames to %s\n",
				z80.Cartridge.Name, len(g.tape), *rec)
		}
	}
	// A disk keeps what was written to it. Games with a level editor on
	// them -- which is why disks are supported at all -- save through the
	// same disk function calls they load through, and the image those
	// reach is this one. It is written beside the snapshot rather than
	// over the original, so the floppy msx2go converted stays as it was.
	if m.Disk != nil {
		if e := m.DOSFlushAll(); e != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%s: %v\n", z80.Cartridge.Name, e)
		}
		if m.Disk.Dirty() {
			p := *disk
			if p == "" {
				p = z80.Cartridge.Name + ".dsk"
			}
			if e := os.WriteFile(p, m.Disk.Image(), 0o644); e != nil {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%s: %v\n", z80.Cartridge.Name, e)
			} else {
				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%s: the disk changed -> %s\n",
					z80.Cartridge.Name, p)
			}
		}
	}
	if *learn != "" {
		var b strings.Builder
		b.WriteString("# Addresses this build had to interpret, with the " +
			"banks in force.\n")
		for _, l := range m.Learned() {
			b.WriteString(l)
			b.WriteByte('\n')
		}
		if werr := os.WriteFile(*learn, []byte(b.String()), 0o644); werr != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "__NAME__:", werr)
		}
	}
	if err != nil {
		die(err)
	}
}

// game is one MSX: a machine, something to draw its video memory with, and
// somewhere for its sound chip's registers to be heard.
type game struct {
	m     *z80.M
	rend  *z80.Renderer
	img   *ebiten.Image
	snd   *sound
	state  string
	border bool
	dead   bool
	// held keeps F9 and F10 from firing again every frame they are down.
	held map[ebiten.Key]bool
	// rec and tape record what was pressed, a byte a frame.
	rec  bool
	tape []byte
}

// stick is what the joystick port reports. A game usually reads only these,
// and reads them from either the port or the keyboard, so both are driven.
var stick = []struct {
	key ebiten.Key
	bit z80.Buttons
}{
	{ebiten.KeyUp, z80.Up},
	{ebiten.KeyDown, z80.Down},
	{ebiten.KeyLeft, z80.Left},
	{ebiten.KeyRight, z80.Right},
	{ebiten.KeySpace, z80.TriggerA},
	{ebiten.KeyZ, z80.TriggerA},
	{ebiten.KeyShiftLeft, z80.TriggerB},
	{ebiten.KeyX, z80.TriggerB},
}

// keymap is the rest of the keyboard, because a cartridge reads more than a
// joystick's worth: Salamander wants F5 to continue after a game over, and
// menus want RETURN, ESC, STOP and the digits. Every one of these is a
// position in the MSX matrix and costs nothing to provide.
var keymap = []struct {
	key ebiten.Key
	msx z80.MSXKey
}{
	{ebiten.KeyF1, z80.KeyF1}, {ebiten.KeyF2, z80.KeyF2},
	{ebiten.KeyF3, z80.KeyF3}, {ebiten.KeyF4, z80.KeyF4},
	{ebiten.KeyF5, z80.KeyF5},
	{ebiten.KeyEscape, z80.KeyEsc}, {ebiten.KeyTab, z80.KeyTab},
	{ebiten.KeyBackspace, z80.KeyBS}, {ebiten.KeyEnter, z80.KeyReturn},
	{ebiten.KeyControlLeft, z80.KeyCtrl},
	{ebiten.KeyHome, z80.KeyHome}, {ebiten.KeyInsert, z80.KeyIns},
	{ebiten.KeyDelete, z80.KeyDel},
	// The MSX STOP key, which has no obvious host equivalent.
	{ebiten.KeyPause, z80.KeyStop},
	// The directions and the two triggers again, so that a game reading the
	// matrix rather than the port sees the same thing.
	{ebiten.KeyUp, z80.KeyUp}, {ebiten.KeyDown, z80.KeyDown},
	{ebiten.KeyLeft, z80.KeyLeft}, {ebiten.KeyRight, z80.KeyRight},
	{ebiten.KeySpace, z80.KeySpace}, {ebiten.KeyZ, z80.KeySpace},
	{ebiten.KeyShiftLeft, z80.KeySelect}, {ebiten.KeyX, z80.KeySelect},
}

// Update runs exactly one frame of the cartridge, which is one interrupt.
func (g *game) Update() error {
	if g.dead {
		return nil
	}
	var b z80.Buttons
	for _, k := range stick {
		if ebiten.IsKeyPressed(k.key) {
			b |= k.bit
		}
	}
	if g.rec {
		g.tape = append(g.tape, byte(b))
	}
	g.m.SetJoystick(b)
	g.m.ClearKeys()
	for _, k := range keymap {
		if ebiten.IsKeyPressed(k.key) {
			g.m.PressKey(k.msx)
		}
	}
	// The letters and digits, for anything that asks by name.
	for c := byte('A'); c <= 'Z'; c++ {
		if ebiten.IsKeyPressed(ebiten.KeyA + ebiten.Key(c-'A')) {
			if k, ok := z80.LetterKey(c); ok {
				g.m.PressKey(k)
			}
		}
	}
	for c := byte('0'); c <= '9'; c++ {
		if ebiten.IsKeyPressed(ebiten.KeyDigit0 + ebiten.Key(c-'0')) {
			if k, ok := z80.DigitKey(c); ok {
				g.m.PressKey(k)
			}
		}
	}
	if err := g.m.Frame(); err != nil {
		g.dead = true
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "__NAME__:", err)
		return err
	}
	// Between frames, which is the only place a snapshot is meaningful: a
	// frame is one call into the translated code, and once it has returned
	// there is no Go control flow left to preserve. See
	// runtime/snapshot.go.
	g.hotkeys()
	// The sound driver writes the chip's registers once a frame, so once a
	// frame is when the synthesiser needs to hear about them. Anything
	// finer would be inventing timing the cartridge never had.
	g.snd.frame(&g.m.PSG)
	return nil
}

// hotkeys are the harness's own: F9 saves a snapshot, F10 restores one, F11
// fills the screen, and F12 puts the next floppy in the drive for a game
// that shipped on more than one. They act on the press rather than for as
// long as the key is held, and none of them is a key an MSX has, so none is
// taken from the cartridge.
func (g *game) hotkeys() {
	if g.held == nil {
		g.held = map[ebiten.Key]bool{}
	}
	for _, k := range []ebiten.Key{ebiten.KeyF9, ebiten.KeyF10,
		ebiten.KeyF11, ebiten.KeyF12} {
		down := ebiten.IsKeyPressed(k)
		if down && !g.held[k] {
			switch k {
			case ebiten.KeyF9:
				g.save()
			case ebiten.KeyF10:
				g.load()
			case ebiten.KeyF11:
				ebiten.SetFullscreen(!ebiten.IsFullscreen())
			case ebiten.KeyF12:
				g.swap()
			}
		}
		g.held[k] = down
	}
}

// swap answers an "insert disk 2" prompt: the next floppy goes in the
// drive, and round again after the last one.
func (g *game) swap() {
	if g.m.Images() < 2 {
		return
	}
	n := g.m.SwapNext(0)
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "__NAME__: inserted %s\n", g.m.ImageName(n))
}

func (g *game) save() {
	f, err := os.Create(g.state)
	if err == nil {
		err = g.m.SaveState(f, z80.Cartridge.SHA1)
		if cerr := f.Close(); err == nil {
			err = cerr
		}
	}
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "__NAME__: snapshot:", err)
		return
	}
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "__NAME__: snapshot saved to "+g.state)
}

func (g *game) load() {
	f, err := os.Open(g.state)
	if err == nil {
		err = g.m.LoadState(f, z80.Cartridge.SHA1)
		f.Close()
	}
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "__NAME__: restore:", err)
		return
	}
	// The restored machine has register state and no write history, so
	// the synthesiser has to adopt the chip wholesale. See Synth.Prime.
	g.snd.prime(&g.m.PSG)
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "__NAME__: restored from "+g.state)
}

// Draw blits what the video memory says. Rendering is a pure function of VRAM
// and the registers, so this is the only part of the program that knows
// anything about a window.
func (g *game) Draw(screen *ebiten.Image) {
	img := g.rend.RenderVDP(&g.m.VDP)
	// The picture is 192 lines or 212, depending on what the cartridge
	// asked register 9 for, and it can change while the game runs -- Space
	// Manbow's intro is 192 and its stages are 212. So the texture follows
	// the image rather than assuming.
	h := img.Bounds().Dy()
	// The width follows the image for the same reason the height does:
	// SCREEN 6 and SCREEN 7 are 512 dots across, and a texture made 256
	// wide is handed twice the pixels it has room for.
	w := img.Bounds().Dx()
	if g.img == nil || g.img.Bounds().Dy() != h || g.img.Bounds().Dx() != w {
		g.img = ebiten.NewImage(w, h)
	}
	g.img.WritePixels(img.Pix)

	// A dot is not a square, and in the wide modes it is not even the same
	// shape as in the narrow ones. SCREEN 6 and SCREEN 7 put 512 dots
	// across the *same* piece of glass that SCREEN 5 puts 256 across, so
	// the dots are half as wide -- the picture does not get wider. Drawing
	// a 512-dot mode into a wider frame is what made it look stretched
	// beside a real machine.
	//
	// So the layout is one fixed size, two of everything: 512 dots and
	// twice the lines, whatever mode is running. A narrow picture is drawn
	// at double width into it and a wide one at single, and both come out
	// the shape the hardware makes them. It is the size openMSX settles on
	// for the same reason.
	sx := float64(z80.ScreenWidthWide) / float64(w)
	var op ebiten.DrawImageOptions
	op.GeoM.Scale(sx, 2)
	if !g.border {
		screen.DrawImage(g.img, &op)
		return
	}
	// The surround the hardware draws, in the colour register 7 is set to
	// right now -- games change it, and some flash it, so it is read every
	// frame rather than once.
	screen.Fill(g.m.VDP.BorderRGBA())
	op.GeoM.Translate(z80.BorderLeft*2, float64(z80.FrameHeight-h)) // (F-h)/2, doubled
	screen.DrawImage(g.img, &op)
	_ = image.Rect
}

// Layout is the same size whatever mode is running: wide enough for the most
// dots any mode has, and twice the lines. See Draw -- a wide mode has smaller
// dots, not a bigger picture, and a layout that grew with the dot count told
// ebiten to stretch the frame instead.
func (g *game) Layout(int, int) (int, int) {
	if g.border {
		return z80.FrameWidth * 2, z80.FrameHeight * 2
	}
	h := z80.ScreenHeight
	if g.rend.Lines() > h {
		h = g.rend.Lines()
	}
	return z80.ScreenWidthWide, h * 2
}

// sampleRate is what the audio context runs at.
const sampleRate = 44100

// sound is the chips, a lock, and the samples waiting to be played.
//
// The samples are made on the *emulation's* clock -- one frame's worth every
// time a frame runs -- and not on the sound card's. Those are two independent
// clocks, and generating on the card's meant a buffer covered two frames of
// register changes one time and three the next, which modulates when every
// note starts. It is heard as the music slowing down and speeding up and
// slowing down again, in time with the beat between the two rates. Made a
// frame at a time, a frame is always worth exactly the same number of
// samples and the tempo cannot wander; what is left of the difference
// between the clocks is a buffer that fills a little faster or slower than
// it drains, which is what the high and low water marks below are for.
type sound struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	synth *z80.Synth
	// scc is the chip in the cartridge's own mapper, where there is one.
	// It plays over the PSG rather than instead of it, which is what the
	// hardware does: two chips, one speaker.
	scc *z80.SCC

	// perFrame is how many stereo samples one emulated frame is worth.
	// At the standard sixty frames a second that is 735.
	perFrame int
	// ring holds them until the card asks, oldest first, interleaved.
	ring []int16
	// last is the pair most recently played, held when the ring runs dry
	// so that an underrun is a moment of stillness rather than a click to
	// silence and back.
	last [2]int16
	// primed says the ring has built up its cushion and playing has
	// begun. Without one the two clocks settle at an empty buffer, where
	// every wobble in either of them is an underrun; with one they settle
	// around the cushion instead, and it absorbs them. It is cleared
	// again if the ring ever does run dry, so a game that was paused for
	// a minute builds its cushion back rather than stuttering into it.
	primed bool
}

// cushion is how much sound is kept ahead of the card: three frames, fifty
// milliseconds, which is short enough not to be felt and long enough to
// cover the difference between a timer and a crystal.
func (s *sound) cushion() int { return s.perFrame * 2 * 3 }

func newSound(m *z80.M, perFrame int) *sound {
	// Recording the writes, rather than reading the register file back, is
	// the whole of what the synthesiser needs to hear. See frame.
	m.PSG.Log = true
	if perFrame < 1 {
		perFrame = 1
	}
	sy := z80.NewSynth(sampleRate)
	// Whatever the boot left in the chip: the writes from before this
	// moment are not in the log, and a driver sets some registers only
	// once. See Synth.Prime.
	sy.Prime(m.PSG.Reg)
	return &sound{synth: sy, scc: &m.SCC, perFrame: perFrame}
}

// frame hands the synthesiser the writes the driver actually made, in order,
// and then makes exactly one frame's worth of sound out of them.
//
// Pushing the whole register file once a frame instead sounds nearly right
// and is wrong in one audible way: register 13 is the envelope shape, and
// writing it *restarts the envelope*. Re-writing it sixty times a second
// retriggers whatever the envelope was doing sixty times a second, which
// turns a decaying note into a buzz and a silence into a rasp -- and Konami's
// drivers use envelope-shaped percussion, so it is not a corner case.
//
// A write is an event, not a state. The machine records them in order and
// this drains them.
// prime adopts the chip's registers, for a machine that has just been
// restored from a snapshot.
func (s *sound) prime(p *z80.PSG) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	p.TakeWrites()
	s.synth.Prime(p.Reg)
}

func (s *sound) frame(p *z80.PSG) {
	w := p.TakeWrites()
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	for _, x := range w {
		s.synth.Write(x.Reg, x.Val)
	}
	buf := make([]int16, s.perFrame*2)
	s.synth.Synthesize(buf)
	s.scc.Synthesize(buf)
	s.ring = append(s.ring, buf...)
	// A card that has stopped asking -- a window with no focus, a machine
	// suspended -- must not grow this without bound. A quarter of a second
	// is far more than the latency anything needs, and dropping the oldest
	// keeps what is about to be heard rather than what should have been.
	if high := s.perFrame * 2 * 15; len(s.ring) > high {
		s.ring = append(s.ring[:0], s.ring[len(s.ring)-high:]...)
	}
}

// Read fills a buffer with signed 16-bit stereo, which is what the audio
// context asks for.
func (s *sound) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
	n := len(p) / 4 * 4
	want := n / 2
	buf := make([]int16, want)
	s.mu.Lock()
	if !s.primed {
		if len(s.ring) < s.cushion() {
			s.mu.Unlock()
			// Silence, and quietly: nothing has been played yet, so
			// there is nothing to hold.
			for i := range p[:n] {
				p[i] = 0
			}
			return n, nil
		}
		s.primed = true
	}
	got := copy(buf, s.ring)
	if got < want {
		s.primed = false
	}
	s.ring = append(s.ring[:0], s.ring[got:]...)
	if got >= 2 {
		s.last[0], s.last[1] = buf[got-2], buf[got-1]
	}
	// Short: the frames have not been run yet, because the game is paused
	// or the window is not being drawn. Holding the last pair keeps the
	// speaker where it was instead of snapping it to zero and back.
	for i := got; i+1 < want; i += 2 {
		buf[i], buf[i+1] = s.last[0], s.last[1]
	}
	s.mu.Unlock()
	for i, v := range buf {
		p[i*2] = byte(v)
		p[i*2+1] = byte(v >> 8)
	}
	return n, nil
}

// startAudio gives the cartridge's sound somewhere to go. A machine with no
// device still plays the game.
func startAudio(s *sound) {
	ctx := eaudio.NewContext(sampleRate)
	p, err := ctx.NewPlayer(s)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "__NAME__: no audio:", err)
		return
	}
	p.SetBufferSize(50 * time.Millisecond)
	p.Play()
}

func die(err error) {
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "__NAME__:", err)
	os.Exit(1)
}
